findings.reason: the §6 retirement list must either name the `batched_labeller` call sites to reroute onto `solve.fixed_point` or exclude the shared reduced-state program kernels from the deletion, before `reduced_newton.py` can be removed.
findings.text: §6 (`converged-forward-solve.html` §6, "Retirement") lists `reduced_newton.py` for deletion, but `batched_labeller.py` binds it at module level to `_BACKTRACKING_FACTORS`, `FixedPointTerminationReason`, `_row_augmentation`, `_compiled_program`, `_reduced_kernels`, `reduced_coordinates` and `_RowArguments` (lines 133–653) plus the `FIXED_POINT_RESIDUAL_TOLERANCE`/`NEWTON_STEPS`/`ACTIVE_SET_STEPS` constants, and is exercised by `tests/test_batched_labeller.py`, `tests/test_labeller_parallel.py` and `benchmarks/batched_labeller_receipt.py`, so the deletion leaves a live, separately-owned batch-solver consumer broken; the design document's consumer audit (design line 179) names inverse, transport and media but omits the labeller.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — four pure functions each hide substantial behaviour behind a small interface: `topology.read` (field representation, sub-cell membership, normal-form saddle support, one differentiable null evaluator), `current.book` (exact-clip booking and quadrature), `gs.apply` (the map plus the implicit Picard, moment-map and boundary-flux-envelope derivatives), `solve.fixed_point` (Newton-GMRES on the map's own JVP through one fixed-capacity scan).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 retires `reduced_newton.py`, but that module is shared infrastructure consumed by `nova/equilibrium/batched_labeller.py`, whose import the plan does not name.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (supplied 2026-10-05T17:47:40Z); each of §2–§5 names in its own text what it retires (Topology.read/read_with_connectivity; `clipped_support_current_moments` plus the `forward_operator.py` support partition; the `ForwardFluxOperator` map; `newton_krylov`/`picard`/`operator_request_body`), so no section adds to a counted family without accounting for the surface it removes.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan and its design inventory bind 40 existing implementations (17 null-role, 23 region-role) to a destination each, and the two most recent prior reviews folded concrete reuse candidates into §5 (`_single_site_krylov`, `_krylov_machine`, `_serve_krylov_stream`, `_krylov_outputs`, `_steepest_descent_promotion` — verified present at `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py:2619,2216,2394,2371,1672`) and §2 (`nova/biot/null.py`, `nova/biot/fieldnull.py` — verified present); the shipped `coefficient-space-newton` route (`nova/equilibrium/coefficient_carrier.py`, `plan-status: shipped`, arm B "a measured trade rather than a win") is a concluded measured-loser, not a reuse candidate, so its absence from the inventory is not a gap.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §6 states `gs.apply` "replaces the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs today rather than wrapping it" (`nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:2323`), and §5 relocates `fixed_point.py`'s single-site kernel into `solve.py` behind one call site rather than layering a wrapper; no unjustified thin layer is added over existing machinery.
